solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Don’t change way in which core is removed (4)

indicatorNotes.in which core is removed: the core of a word is its middle, so its middle letters go

blocks.note: a street is a way, as in road names
the two central letters of STREET are taken out

annotation.surface: An instruction to leave some method alone after a heart has been taken out of it.
annotation.walkthrough: STET is the proofreader's mark meaning 'let it stand', written beside a correction that should be ignored.
annotation.definitionFit: Stet is Latin for 'let it stand', telling a printer not to change the text.

entries.clue: Award-winning picture: Selfie with His Majesty? (3,4,3,1)

blocks.note: the 1956 musical film won five Oscars
a selfie shows me, and here the king is in it too

annotation.surface: A prize-winning photo that turns out to be someone posing beside the monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picture' wants to be a photograph, which the selfie supports; it is a film. The question mark flags the playful second reading.
annotation.definitionFit: The King and I is a film, and films are pictures that win awards.

entries.clue: Chunter on about club (9)

indicatorNotes.about: about can mean turned around, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone muttering endlessly about their golf or social club.
annotation.walkthrough: To chunter is British for to grumble under your breath. 'About' reads as 'on the subject of', but it is shaking up the nine letters before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short heavy club carried by British police officers.

entries.clue: A danger VAT put off artistic pioneers (5-5)

indicatorNotes.put off: put off can mean disturbed, so the letters are knocked out of order

annotation.surface: Experimental artists deterred by the threat of a sales tax on their work.
annotation.walkthrough: VAT is the UK's sales tax, which makes 'put off' read as discouraged; it is the signal to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: The avant-garde are the artists who push ahead of the mainstream.

entries.clue: Three articles Penny found in soldier’s quarters (3,4)

blocks.note: AN, THE and A are all articles

annotation.surface: A soldier's barracks where someone turned up three items and a coin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' is the soldier ant, a worker caste that defends the nest, so its quarters are an ant heap rather than a barracks.
annotation.definitionFit: Soldier ants live in the nest, so an ant heap is where a soldier is quartered.

entries.clue: Hubris in sailor just the start of navy’s awful, awful year (5,10)

indicatorNotes.just the start of: only the opening letter of the next word is taken
indicatorNotes.awful: the first 'awful' says the letters are in a terrible state, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: A proud seaman's pride brings the navy a dreadful twelve months.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Awful' is written twice: the first scrambles the fodder, the second begins the definition. The Queen called 1992 her annus horribilis, Latin for 'horrible year'.
annotation.definitionFit: Annus horribilis is Latin for a horrible year, famously the Queen's phrase for 1992.

entries.clue: Work in that place is cause of death (3,4)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece is placed inside the other

annotation.surface: A warning that working somewhere will kill you.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'work' a job that kills you; it is a single musical piece. 'The rope' is the hangman's noose, as in 'facing the rope'.
annotation.definitionFit: The rope means hanging, so it is the cause of death for the condemned.

entries.clue: Aggressive Trump broadcast (5)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: broadcast means sent out as sound, so the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: to ruff is to play a trump card in bridge or whist

annotation.surface: A news report on an aggressive Donald Trump.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Trump the president; he is a card-game verb. RUFF and ROUGH are said the same way.
annotation.definitionFit: Rough play is aggressive play, as in a rough tackle.

entries.clue: Arrive in middle of Manhattan, out of cash at first (5)

indicatorNotes.out of: out of means without, so a letter is removed
indicatorNotes.at first: only the first letter of cash is meant

blocks.note: center is the American spelling of centre, fitting Manhattan
the first letter of cash, which is taken out

annotation.surface: Turning up in midtown New York with no money at the start of a trip.
annotation.walkthrough: Manhattan is there to say the middle should be spelt the American way, CENTER, so that removing C leaves ENTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: coming into a room or a city is arriving there.

entries.clue: Hesitancy spoilt ANC lecture (10)

indicatorNotes.spoilt: a spoilt thing has been damaged out of its proper form

annotation.surface: A nervous speaker ruins a talk to the African National Congress.
annotation.walkthrough: The ANC is South Africa's governing party, but here its letters are just fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Reluctance is unwillingness to act, which is hesitancy.

entries.clue: Old writer’s lines thrown out. Time to give up? (4)

indicatorNotes.thrown out: thrown out means removed, so the named letters go

blocks.note: QUILL, an old pen, loses LL (lines)

annotation.surface: An aging author whose verses were rejected wonders whether to retire.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'old writer' is a pen, not an author. L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: quitting smoking or a job means abandoning it, which is giving up.

entries.clue: Learner infiltrating enchanter’s group (6)

indicatorNotes.infiltrating: to infiltrate is to get inside

blocks.note: Circe, the enchantress of the Odyssey

annotation.surface: A trainee sneaking into a wizard's coven.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's joins the wordplay to the definition, so 'group' is not owned by the enchanter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a social set of friends or colleagues is called their circle.

entries.clue: Footwear from the east nearly here — it’s quite something (8)

indicatorNotes.from the east: in an across clue, read from the east means right to left
indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

annotation.surface: Someone announcing that a remarkable pair of shoes from the Orient has almost arrived.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From the east' sounds like where the shoes were made; it tells you to read CROCS backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang a scorcher is something remarkable, whether a very hot day or a stunning shot.

entries.clue: Project to repeal tax abandoned (11)

indicatorNotes.abandoned: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

annotation.surface: A government scheme to scrap a tax has been dropped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Project' reads as a noun, a scheme, but the answer is the verb: to project a trend forward.
annotation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to project known figures forward to estimate what comes next.

entries.clue: Villa guest nursing a fever (4)

indicatorNotes.nursing: nursing means holding, so the answer is held inside the words

annotation.surface: A holiday visitor at a villa laid up with a fever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nursing' fits the sick guest so well that it hides its job of holding the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An ague is an old word for a fever with shivering fits.

entries.clue: Bent on tipsy rep being sacked (10)

indicatorNotes.tipsy: part of the fodder, not an indicator
indicatorNotes.being sacked: sacked can mean plundered and wrecked, so the letters are thrown about

annotation.surface: A boss determined to fire a drunken sales representative.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tipsy' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'being sacked' does the shuffling.
annotation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination, which is a propensity.

entries.clue: What’s lost in era of the psychiatrist? (9)

blocks.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist

annotation.surface: Asking what has been forgotten in the age of therapy.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces go in reverse clue order: the psychiatrist first, then the era. Shrinkage is the retail word for stock lost to theft or damage.
annotation.definitionFit: Shrinkage is the amount lost, as in stock that goes missing from a shop.

entries.clue: Dull Republican trapped in loveless marriage worked for CIA? (10)

indicatorNotes.loveless: love is O, the zero score in tennis, and -less removes it
indicatorNotes.trapped in: one piece is held inside another

annotation.surface: A boring politician stuck in a cold marriage turns out to have been a spy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loveless' reads as a cold relationship; it strips the O out, since love is zero in tennis scoring.
annotation.definitionFit: Uninspired means lacking spark, which is dull.

entries.clue: Disrespectful of a European academic to take precedence (7)

indicatorNotes.to take precedence: to take precedence is to go first, so this piece is placed at the front

blocks.note: an is the form of the article a before a vowel

annotation.surface: Complaining that a professor from Europe insists on going first.
annotation.walkthrough: The academic is written last but told to go in front. The article 'a' becomes its other form, since the next letter is a vowel.
annotation.definitionFit: Profane means showing disrespect for sacred things.

entries.clue: Idle cop took drugs, boss finally admitted (7)

indicatorNotes.finally: only the last letter of boss is taken
indicatorNotes.admitted: admitted means let in, so this letter goes inside

blocks.note: to use is to take drugs

annotation.surface: A lazy police officer who took drugs, as his superior eventually confessed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Admitted' reads as confessed; it tells you to let S into DI USED. A DI is a British police rank.
annotation.definitionFit: Something disused is no longer used, so it lies idle.

entries.clue: Outspoken radical examined (4)

indicatorNotes.Outspoken: spoken out loud, so the word is heard rather than seen

blocks.note: a red is a political radical

annotation.surface: A blunt revolutionary has been scrutinized.
annotation.walkthrough: The past tense READ is said like RED. 'Outspoken' looks like it describes the radical.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: going through a report closely is studying, or examining, it.

entries.clue: A few ticks and I’ll be off (4,4)

annotation.definition: A few ticks and I’ll be off

blocks.note: reads as the British 'in a tick', a moment; meant as the literal ticks of a clock mechanism
reads as leaving; meant as exploding, the way an alarm or a charge goes off

annotation.surface: Someone saying they will leave in a moment.
annotation.walkthrough: The speaker is a device counting down with a clockwork timer, and when the ticking stops it detonates.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue is spoken by the device: its clock ticks for a while, then it explodes.

entries.clue: Scandalous information circulating about American gang (5)

indicatorNotes.circulating: going round, so the word turns back on itself
indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so this word surrounds the next

blocks.note: dirt is scandal, as in digging up dirt
A = American, placed inside the turned word

annotation.surface: Gossip going round about an American criminal outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: A goes between TRI and D. A triad is a Chinese criminal gang.
annotation.definitionFit: A triad is a Chinese organized-crime gang.

entries.clue: Money matters (5)

blocks.note: wealth, as in a person who lives beyond their resources
a verb: is important to someone, as in 'your friendship ___ a lot'

annotation.walkthrough: Read together it is a heading about finance; split, it is a noun and a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Means is wealth, and to mean something to someone is to matter to them.

entries.clue: High-ranking gentleman from Ibiza controlling island (6)

indicatorNotes.controlling: to control something is to hold it, so this word holds the next

blocks.note: señor is Spanish for gentleman, and Ibiza is Spanish

annotation.surface: An important Spanish man who is in charge of an island.
annotation.walkthrough: Ibiza is there only to make the gentleman Spanish.
annotation.definitionFit: Senior means higher in rank.

entries.clue: Country queen giving one new position (4)

indicatorNotes.giving one new position: the letter I (one) is moved to a new place in the word

blocks.note: a rani is an Indian queen
the I of the queen moves to the front

annotation.surface: A rural monarch promoting someone to a new job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective for the queen, as in country house; it is the definition. Only the one letter I moves.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Iran is one country among many, the Middle Eastern state once called Persia.

entries.clue: Crafty individual, likely to go far in the main? (4,6)

annotation.definition2: likely to go far in the main?

blocks.note: a seaman works on a craft, and 'able' is skilful

blocks.clueFragment: likely to go far in the main?
blocks.note: the main is the open sea, where sailors travel far

annotation.surface: A cunning person who is tipped to succeed, on the whole.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' means cunning but also 'of boats', and 'in the main' means mostly but also on the high seas. An able seaman is a navy rank.
annotation.definitionFit: An able seaman is a trained sailor, a person on a craft who sails far across the main.

entries.clue: Not happy place is charging sick (10)

indicatorNotes.is charging: to charge something is to load it, so this piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: PL = place, as in street names

annotation.surface: An unhappy patient complaining that the clinic bills them for being ill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charging' sounds like billing; it means loading, as a gun is charged.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone annoyed or dissatisfied is not happy.

entries.clue: Always back party shunning right wing (4)

indicatorNotes.shunning right wing: the right-hand end of the word is avoided, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.back: back means backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the right-hand end of REVEL, which is shunned

annotation.surface: A loyal member who keeps supporting a party that has turned its back on the right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' and 'right wing' make a political picture; the party is a celebration and the right wing is the end letter of REVEL.
annotation.definitionFit: Ever means always, as in 'ever faithful'.
